To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LV can learn from noisy images and that it can learn recursive background theories that are themselves capable of identifying ambiguities.

(a) LV is capable of learning recursive theories of light from noisy images and (b) the resulting theory is capable of identifying the position of hidden light sources and the position of the RoboCUp ball.

(i) the new noise- and attribute-robust version one-shot LV can achieve at least comparable performance to statistical machine learners on both prediction of the position of hidden light sources and the position of the football, (ii) the one-shot version of LV can learn a recursive theory of light and use it to identify the position of the hidden light sources in telescopic and microscopy images, and the position of a hidden ball in RoboCup images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of MIL to learn logic programs that are able to reason about the existence, position and other features of objects in real images.
the use of ILP to address problems where statistical machine learning is not appropriate, and where it is important to be able to reason below the level of the classification.

the development and application of a novel machine learning approach to image analysis that can be used to learn a variety of high-level concepts from small numbers of noisy images, and that can be used for reasoning about the image beyond simple classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

LV can achieve high-accuracy classification with a single example and can also provide reasoning about objects and their position in the image, including the existence of light sources and objects not directly in the image.

LV has been extended to noisy images and has demonstrated comparable performance to a statistical machine learner on real data, while also providing a more transparent, human-interpretable, and more generalisable representation.

the new noise- robust LV is able to achieve a comparable level of accuracy to a thirty-shot machine learning system on real noisy images with a single example, and is able to reason below the level of image classification to provide information about subobjects and the position of light sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we demonstrate a new approach to image classification that can learn a general recursive background theory and can be applied to a single noisy example, and can be used to reason beyond classification.

LV can be used to predict the existence and position in the image of objects and sub-objects with high accuracy, and to identify the position of light sources, even when the image is noisy and the number of examples is small.

LV is capable of high- accuracy prediction of classes such that statistical machine learners give near-random predictions, and that LV is able to provide reasoning about secondary properties of the image that are not available to statistical machine learners.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple, noise-robust, one-shot inductive logic programming approach to image classification can achieve comparable accuracy to state-of-the-art statistical machine learners, and can provide additional support for secondary reasoning.

the combination of MIL and low-level primitive-level image processing is a viable alternative to deep learning and statistical machine learning for image classification and reasoning in the presence of noise.
MIL is able to achieve high accuracy in image classification using a small number of noisy images, while also providing support for secondary reasoning below the level classification.
